functionality.rationale: Selecting the wrong policy source could reject valid commits or allow a replacement identity to self-authorize.

security.rationale: A mutable trust root lets an untrusted commit redefine the attribution policy that judges that same commit.

performance.rationale: The check reads one small blob and one commit path list per governed commit.

compatibility.rationale: The initial activation and pre-policy history must remain valid while later policy changes are rejected.

concurrency.rationale: Validation reads immutable commit objects and introduces no shared mutable state.

platform.rationale: Git blob and diff-tree queries must behave consistently across supported development hosts.

persistence.rationale: The change makes the committed identity policy a permanent repository trust root.

adr.rationale: This hardens an existing internal Git policy without changing a public product contract.

architecture.rationale: Runtime modules and dependency directions are unchanged.

roadmap.rationale: Repository attribution governance completes no product milestone.
